text:
nina: Hi @people-ops — quick Q: can I add my 30yo brother to my Redwood medical/dental because he lives with me and is disabled + financially dependent? He's not on my taxes.

people-ops: Hi Nina :wave: short answer: maybe. We need to confirm dependent eligibility under our plan and IRS rules. Please DM or use Secure Upload for docs — don't post SSNs here.

nina: Thanks. What docs are acceptable? doctor note? SSDI award letter? proof of residency?

jordan-hr: Hi — for adult dependents with disabilities we typically ask for: a physician statement confirming the disability and that they're unable to self-care, proof of financial support (recent bank transfers or tax docs), proof of shared residence (utility bill or lease), and either an SSDI award letter or court guardianship paperwork. Carriers differ on exact docs.

people-ops: Also note: adding outside Open Enrollment depends on having a Qualifying Life Event (QLE). A change in dependent's disability status can be a QLE if the event is recent; long-standing disabilities may still be eligible but need carrier review. What's the timing on when this started?

nina: He's had the disability for years and has lived with me ~3 years. I didn't claim him on taxes. Is retro coverage possible?

people-ops: Usually we can request retro effective dates back to when paperwork supports coverage, but carriers limit how far back they accept retro enrollments (often 30–60 days). We'll submit to the carrier once we have complete docs. Payroll deductions will be pro-rated from the carrier's effective date.

people-ops: Please use our Secure Upload portal (select "Dependent Eligibility") so PII stays protected: https://redwood.hr/secure-upload

benefits-bot: Automated reminder: upload required docs within 30 days to avoid processing delays. Checklist: https://redwood.hr/dependents-checklist :memo:

nina: Ok I will DM the documents now (no SSN in the thread).

alex: FWIW I added an adult cousin as a dependent last year in a similar situation — carrier took ~2 weeks to confirm. Payroll adjusted in the next pay cycle and they pro-rated prior month. Hang in there! :thumbsup:

people-ops: Thanks @nina — we got the DM. We'll review and follow up here after carrier confirmation. If carrier requires additional paperwork we'll ping you. If approved, payroll will show a pro-rated deduction and any retro premiums will be handled over 1–2 pay cycles.

nina: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick help :heart:

people-ops: No problem. Keeping this thread for the audit trail. If anything changes we'll update.
